1: Build the axle beam. The two turntables are the kingpins the front wheels steer on.
2: One knuckle on each turntable, holes facing sideways. The knuckle should swivel freely.
3: Steering arms: the end holes sit directly over the knuckle; the arm points backwards.
4: The post in front of the knuckles will carry the frame.
5:
Lay the tie rod across the arm studs (it rests ON the studs, it does not press on).
Push a pin down through each end hole into the steering-arm hole behind the knuckle.
6:
The lever sits on top of the tie rod. The 2L axle goes through the lever's end
(axle hole, locked) into the tie rod's centre hole (round, free to turn).
7: Stub axle through each knuckle, then two bushes on the outside.
8: Wheel, then a half bush to hold it on.
9: Press the 4 x 6 plate onto the top of the post.
10:
Two frame rails on the plate. Any 1 x 10 bricks work for this test
(or 1 x 8 + 1 x 2). Keep them 2 studs apart.
11: The bearing plate bridges the rails. Its middle hole must be over the lever's free end.
12: Drop the 4L axle through the bearing into the lever. Joiner, 3L axle and knob on top.
